title: The finite strict Koszul system and its derived-limit presentations
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with topology $J$ and commutative ring sheaf $\mathcal O$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the ring complex $\mathcal O[0]$ of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-extended-cech], and total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For $r\geq0$ and global sections $b:\{0,\ldots,r-1\}\to\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$, define the strict forward diagram $P_m$ as the ordered total tensor of $[\mathcal O\xrightarrow{b_i^{m+1}}\mathcal O]$ in degrees $0,1$, with maps $(1,b_i)$ in each factor. Its degree-zero projections give a cocone to $\mathcal O[0]$; the empty tensor is the constant diagram $\mathcal O[0]$. Define the strict inverse dual tower $Q_m=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P_m,\mathcal O[0])$ by [def-pur-hom-complex] and its unit by dualizing that projection and evaluation at one [def-weil-pbc-ringed-completion-unit]. Define the strict tower complex $T(N)_m=\operatorname{Tot}(N\otimes Q_m)$, with its actual tensor transition maps, by transposing this diagram of complexes degreewise into a complex in $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N^{op},\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O))$. The compatible degree-zero maps give a chain map $N\to\lim_m T(N)_m$ by the degreewise limit universal property. Restrict global sections to every slice by their compatible section families [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction]. A derived-limit presentation consists of a functor $T:D(\mathcal O)\to D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal O))$ with specified localization factorization $QT\cong T(-)Q_{Tow}$, and a total right derived inverse-limit functor with its defining comparison, satisfying the right-derived universal property and computed by inverse limit on K-injective tower complexes [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Its completion functor is the composite; its unit is the preceding ordinary-limit chain map followed by the derived-functor comparison, transported by the specified tensor factorization and representative isomorphisms. Further slice restriction is the exact functor induced by Mathlib overMap, with its canonical overFunctorMap composition isomorphism; its exactness is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction].
